Frame 163 was the sheet with the case-sensitive box over it. The Y landed -- the blank capture that followed it was the screen going dark while the ground was being made, and the guard refused to keep it. I have since read the live screen: I am standing indoors in a golf course service building, Thursday May 20 at 08:00:00, safe mode on, wielding the fishing rod, and the message log says I missed the evacuation.

The list reads eight items, no monsters at all, and forty-four bits of furniture. Golf caps, a golf bag, gloves, tees, balls, a till with fifteen dollars in it -- and glass shards, which means a window went in somewhere.
The list is gone and I can see the room: a shop counter, chairs, lockers, a purple floor under me, and the sidebar reads Thursday May 20, 08:00:00, safe mode on, clear and bright, wielding the rod.

The chart, with a town called West Rutland spread out north of me and my own mark at the bottom of it -- a golf course service building, woods to the south and west, no water anywhere on the whole sheet.
Back in the room, clock still at eight in the morning on Thursday the twentieth, nothing moving.
A box: I have an alarm clock, and it asks whether I want to wait a while or set an alarm for later, with waiting lit.

The wait list: twenty seconds, a minute, five minutes, half an hour, one hour, two, three, six -- and further down, wait till daylight nineteen hours off, till noon four hours, till night eleven hours and fifty-four minutes.
